processing: Details are little documented. It is a green tea with a curled, downy leaf, so expect the usual fixing, rolling and drying of its class.
harvest_season: Made in early spring each year.
appearance_dry: Curled strips with plenty of white down, jade green in colour.
appearance_wet: Tender green leaf, even and tidy.
taste_profile: A high, fresh aroma with a brisk, clean taste and a sweet return.

brewing.notes: Usual practice for downy spring green tea: cooler water and a glass or gaiwan.

vintage_note: An early spring tea, and as with other Chinese greens it is usually sold as the current year's harvest and best drunk within about a year. It is seldom seen outside China, so check the maker and picking date.
description:
Zhenlei Chun is a modern green tea from Zhenlei Shan in the Xinyang area of Henan, the same corner of China that gives us Xinyang Maojian. It is a small regional name, often listed among Henan's notable teas.

It is picked in early spring. The finished leaf is curled and covered in white down, a bright jade green. Exact steps are little documented, but the look points to the ordinary green tea sequence of fixing, rolling and drying.

The liquor is pale green and bright, with a high, fresh aroma and a brisk taste that turns sweet afterwards. Brew it like other tender greens, with water well off the boil.

Its sibling Zhenlei Jianhao is sword-shaped and also heavily downy, so the two are easy to tell apart by leaf shape. If you enjoy this and want a benchmark from the same region, compare it with a Xinyang Maojian.
history: The Xinyang district tea experimental farm in Henan developed it in 1988, alongside Zhenlei Jianhao, as part of a series of new named teas. In 1990 it was rated a famous tea of Henan province.
